A toasted slice of bread is a simple pleasure and is often the subtle touch a meal needs. That’s one reason the humble toaster remains a mainstay in many kitchens, even in the age of air fryers.

Toasters typically achieve doneness using time and temperature. The recently launched Breville Eye Q 850 Auto Toaster swaps those imperfect elements for a more modern approach. The Eye Q uses a pulsing internal sensor to watch the color of the bread as it toasts, only finishing when it hits the perfect result, at least in theory.

title: iFixit tears down iPhone 18 Pro, explores variable aperture, finds concerning repair issue
snippet: iFixit has published its traditional teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro, which shows the variable aperture mechanism up close and explores a potential issue involving display repairs. Watch it below. more…
fullText:
iFixit has published its traditional teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro, which shows the variable aperture mechanism up close and explores a potential issue involving display repairs. Watch it below.

iFixit worries about possible display frame issue

iFixit’s teardown of the iPhone 18 Pro is now live, exploring not just the variable aperture, this year’s biggest camera upgrade, but also the device’s larger vapor chamber, the new under-display Face ID camera, and more.

When it comes to the variable aperture mechanism, iFixit notes that its six tiny blades are controlled by electromagnets, much like the optical image stabilization system, though the two mechanisms operate independently.

During the teardown, one of the tiny aperture blades flew out as iFixit dismantled the lens stack, underscoring how impractical a component-level repair would be. The group says that if the aperture gets stuck, it would likely require replacing the entire main camera assembly.

Another highlight of the new iPhone 18 Pro is its under-display Face ID infrared camera. For this year’s Pro devices, Apple moved the infrared camera beneath the display, while keeping the selfie camera and IR dot projector within the smaller Dynamic Island.

Under a microscope, iFixit found that Apple hides the relocated infrared camera by removing every other row of pixels above the sensor. iFixit notes that the effect fades toward the edges, and that there is an IR-pass filter beneath the OLED layer to block visible light.

Interestingly, the filter doesn’t extend all the way to the edge of the opening, creating what iFixit describes as an “eclipse effect” under certain microscope settings.

As for the iPhone 18 Pro’s bigger vapor chamber, the teardown offers a closer look at Apple’s redesigned cooling architecture.

As the company explained during its “Surprise and Shine” event, the A20 Pro uses a new package that places the silicon die side-by-side with the memory, removing the latter from the SoC’s thermal path and allowing the chip to connect directly to the vapor chamber. Apple also said the new vapor chamber has three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro.

iFixit’s teardown lets us see that setup up close, including the thermal material that presses the A20 Pro directly against the vapor chamber and the chamber itself extending across much of the phone’s body.

Now for the concerning part: iFixit says the plastic frame around the display was damaged on three of the four iPhones its team opened.

While the group notes that other iPhone 18 Pro teardowns haven’t encountered the same issue, and that Apple has been using this same plastic frame since the iPhone 15 Pro, it says it’s too early to tell whether this was an anomaly or a broader repairability concern.

iFixit also suggests that the device’s improved thermal system may be drawing heat away from the display as the heating pad tries to soften the adhesive.

Be that as it may, in practice, as iFixIt explains in the video, a cracked frame means the display may no longer sit perfectly flush after reassembly, and could compromise the phone’s water resistance.

Add to that the fact that some components remain difficult to reach, particularly the USB-C port, which iFixit says requires removing much of the phone’s internals to replace, and DIY repairs of the iPhone 18 Pro may prove challenging depending on which component needs replacing.

All in all, iFixit says the iPhone 18 Pro carries over many of the same repairability strengths and weaknesses as last year’s model, including the glue-free battery tray and modular camera assemblies, but also the need to enter through the display for most major repairs.

For now, the group has given both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max a provisional repairability score of 7 out of 10 as it waits for parts, conducts more tests, and watches whether the display frame issue proves widespread.

Once you’re done, make sure you catch 9to5Mac’s review of the iPhone 18 Pro.

title: Pixel Now Playing update brings interface tweaks & notifications [U]
snippet: The next wave of Pixel app updates is starting with Google rolling out the latest version of Now Playing with interface tweaks. more…
fullText:
The next wave of Pixel app updates is starting with Google rolling out the latest version of Now Playing with interface tweaks.

Update 9/17: Following a server-side update, Now Playing 2026.08.27x and Android System Intelligence C.6 reintroduces Recognized Music Notifications. These silent alerts let you see what’s playing without having to open the app or checking the Quick Settings Tile. Expanding the notification lets you jump to the History tab and favorite songs.

Enabled by default, you can disable them in Now Playing Settings > Notifications.

Original 9/2: When tapping on an identified song’s three-dot button, Now Playing slides up a bottom sheet. This replaces the floating menu and is better for one-handed navigation.

	

You’ll see track information with side-by-side buttons for Share, Add to favorites, and Remove from history. This is followed by a button to play the song and any shortcuts specific to your connected music service.

Meanwhile, the Favorites tab now includes dates and times like the History feed. There are also icon and spacing tweaks in Now Playing Settings.

The redesigned Now Playing launched in March, while Google in April reintroduced the “Tap to see what’s playing” shortcut on the lockscreen.

Version 2026.08.27.x of Pixel Now Playing is widely rolling out via the Google Play Store.

This follows last month’s updates to Pixel Journal that added more tools and Screenshots (extra filter options), as well as new icons for Google Calculator, Clock, Pixel Magnifier, Recorder, and Weather.

title: LinkedIn Adds More Profile Verifications to Combat AI-Powered Job Scams
snippet: Your coworkers and classmates can now vouch that you really do have a specific university or job on your resume.
fullText:
This news is not for people who like to lie on their resume. LinkedIn is adding new ways to verify where you work and went to school, the company announced on Wednesday. The new verifications for members and companies come amid a torrent of AI-powered scams wreaking havoc on social media platforms and the job market. Generative AI makes it easier to create fake media or impersonate specific people, like recruiters or executives.

“With advancements in AI, pretending to be someone that you’re not is getting increasingly cheaper and easier,” Oscar Rodriguez, vice president of LinkedIn’s trust products, told me in an interview. “And with that, authenticity is becoming increasingly important, perhaps more important than it has ever been.” As of September, more than 115 million of LinkedIn’s billion members have added verifications to their profiles. 

	

			

Individual LinkedIn members can verify their current workplace or university by getting two or more colleagues to vouch for them. You’ll need to have been connected to the person vouching for you for at least one year and have two-factor authentication enabled. You won’t be able to vouch for every single person you went to school with or in your office, but those limits are designed to ensure bad actors don’t take advantage of the tool.

Requests to verify your classmates and colleagues will appear under a new, separate section under My Network. LinkedIn says verified accounts see 50% more engagement on their posts and nearly 90% more profile views. 

And if you’re a page admin for a company page on LinkedIn, you can now also remove people falsely claiming to work at your company from LinkedIn’s search results. This is less about cutting down on clout chasers than it is about weeding out scammers who may falsely claim to be a recruiter or executive with a company in order to glean money and personal information from job hunters. Job scams are a growing problem; in a March 2026 survey from the cybersecurity firm Norton, 33% of US respondents said they had encountered a fake recruiter, phishing attempt or fraudulent job posting. Those who fell victim almost always lost money, nearly $9,000 each on average.

How to use LinkedIn’s verification tools

Verification on LinkedIn is free, but it’s a little bit different than other social media platforms. In addition to claiming a person is who they say they are, these tools can also verify where someone goes to school and works. 

Click the down arrow next to your profile picture in the upper-right menu. Click Settings & Privacy.

Click Verifications under Account.

Add verifications for your workplace, education and identity as prompted.

Once you do verify these things, people who view your LinkedIn profile will be prompted to view your verifications when their mouse hovers over your name. You’ll also get an icon that looks like a checkmark inside a shield next to your name. This is the badge you want to look for on company pages when you see a new job listing and get a message from someone claiming to be a recruiter. 

For more info on LinkedIn’s verification tools, check out this help page. You can also read more about LinkedIn’s new AI slop button.

Her work explores how new AI technology is infiltrating our lives, shaping the content we consume on social media and affecting the people behind the screens. She graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill with a degree in media and journalism. You can reach her at kchedraoui@cnet.com.

title: Gmail adds ‘Copy code’ shortcut for 2FA on Android & iOS
snippet: After rolling out Live search and chat earlier this month, Gmail now has a useful “Copy code” button for 2FA on Android and iOS. more…
fullText:
After rolling out Live search and chat earlier this month, Gmail now has a useful “Copy code” button for 2FA on Android and iOS.

Instead of having to open an email to select and copy the two-factor authentication code, Gmail now shows a shortcut directly in your inbox. The pill-shaped “Copy code 000000” button appears below the subject line, like the previews for images, documents, and other attachments.

Tapping the button simply adds the code to your clipboard for a quick paste in the designated app. 

We’ve seen it work for store and banking emails in our brief testing today. It’s a nice quality-of-life addition.

	

The Copy code button is appearing in Gmail for Android (version 2026.09.07.x) and iOS (6.0.260907), but not on the web. This shortcut would also be useful in email notifications on Android.

title: Here’s everything new in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 [Gallery]
snippet: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 is rolling out today to continue the development cycle ahead of the stable December launch. more…
fullText:
Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 is rolling out today to continue the development cycle ahead of the stable December launch.

Over the coming hours, we’ll dive into all of Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5’s new features and every single change. (The newest updates will be at the top of this list. Be sure to check back often and tell us what you find in the comments below.) Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 screenshots appear on the left and Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 on the right.

If you want to quickly install Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 on your compatible Pixel 6a, Pixel 7, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel Tablet, Pixel Fold, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 10a, Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold be sure to check out our step-by-step guide.

Updating…

	

2x Proactive Assistance

On the Pixel 10 and 11 series, we’re seeing a second “Proactive Assistance” menu appear in Settings. The original (as debuted on the Pixel 11) is near the bottom of the list with a blue icon, while the second appears higher with a yellow light bulb icon. Their descriptions are similar, but not identical. The explicit mention of Gemini is the difference.

Blue: “Get personalized suggestions from Gemini at the right time”

Yellow: “Personalized suggestions at the right time”

Blue (original) vs. yellow (QPR2)

From the explanations, both settings pages appear to reference the same capability. Toggling off the original (blue) menu also disables the new switch (yellow).

However, the new menu has a “Use app content for suggestions” page that lets you enable/disable “which apps can share screen content and notifications with Proactive Assistance for suggestions.” There’s also a shortcut to the “Default digital assistant app” page.

This change was first introduced on the Pixel 11 series

Quick Settings: New Audio streams Tile + Layout customization removed

Unclear if layout customization will return before the final QPR2 release, or if Google decided to not proceed with the capability

Additionally, Voice broadcast Tile now under Connectivity instead of system apps

Fixes

Changing a Bluetooth device type in settings failed to update its icon visually. (Issue #516071134)

A system stability issue that caused unexpected device reboots during continuous UI scrolling in media-heavy applications. (Issue #544291113)

Pressing hardware volume buttons while casting media prevented the system volume slider UI from displaying. (Issue #548145018)

Fixed a text-rendering issue that caused unexpected background highlights to appear when typing in search fields, and resolved a navigation routing issue that prevented Private Space from unlocking correctly. (Issue #548285596)

Enhanced HDR mode remained enabled despite being turned off in user settings. (Issue #547457910)

Launching Google Wallet via the power button shortcut caused the touchscreen to become unresponsive. (Issue #549758084)

Camera crashes during panorama processing. (Issue #551069625)

Bluetooth audio experiences noise and distortion after completing or answering a call. (Issue #541684282)
